turns.prompt_text: does Milwaukee or Ryobi make a blowtorch
turns.response_html:
Neither Milwaukee nor Ryobi currently manufactures a dedicated gas-powered blowtorch or propane torch head (like those made by Bernzomatic). Instead, both brands focus on cordless electric heat guns and forced-air propane heaters for high-heat applications.

If you are looking for a tool to generate heat, here is how their current lineups compare:

Electric Heat Tools

For tasks like shrinking tubing, drying materials, or removing adhesives, both brands offer battery-powered heat guns.

  • Milwaukee Compact Heat Gun: This tool is designed for speed, reaching its operational temperature in just 7 seconds. It is highly compact at only 6.4 inches long, making it ideal for tight spaces where a traditional torch might be too dangerous.

  • RYOBI ONE+ 18V Cordless Heat Gun: A more budget-friendly portable option that reaches a maximum temperature of 875°F. It is part of the extensive ONE+ system and includes specialized nozzles for concentrated or deflected heat.

  • RYOBI 18V ONE+ Heat Pen: This is a unique, smaller-scale tool for precision work like crafting or fine electronics, offering dual temperature settings between 450°F and 750°F.

Propane Heat Solutions

While they don't make handheld torches, both brands offer forced-air heaters that run on propane tanks and use power tool batteries to run the fan and igniter:

  • Milwaukee M18 Forced Air Propane Heater: A heavy-duty jobsite heater providing up to 70,000 BTU.
  • Ryobi ONE+ Hybrid Propane Heater: A smaller, hybrid-power option for heating localized workspaces.

Summary Comparison

FeatureMilwaukee (Electric)Ryobi (Electric)
Primary ToolCompact Heat GunHeat Gun / Heat Pen
Max TempApprox. 878°F (470°C)Approx. 875°F

If you specifically need a flame for soldering copper pipes or brazing, you may need to look at a dedicated torch brand like Bernzomatic, as electric heat guns generally do not reach the temperatures required for metalwork.
